To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of specialized representations for statically-typed polymorphic languages is not a problem, and (2) the use of Lisp-like representations for dynamically-typed polymorphic language is not a problem either, as long as one is aware of the problem and does not use them when the type information is available.

(i) the static type system of ML is powerful enough to support efficient data representations; (ii) the implementation of ML is not as difficult as one might think, and can be done by an undergraduate student; (iii) the use of specialized representations is not limited to ML, but is applicable to any statically-typed polymorphic language.

(a) it is possible to use a mix of data representations in the implementation of polymorphic languages and (b) the resulting code is efficient, in the sense that it does not pay the Lisp penalty for data representation.

how to efficiently represent data structures that are polymorphic in their types.
the problem of efficiently representing data in a language with polymorphic types.
how the implementation of a statically typed language can take advantage of the type system to improve the efficiency of its data representations.
